title: Dacarbazine for metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
purpose: Dacarbazine may be used to control metastatic sarcoma and help symptoms. Expected benefit depends on tumour subtype, previous treatment and your overall condition; your consultant explains why this option is appropriate.
schedule: NCCP 00511 gives dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² on day 1 every 21 days. The source describes 4 cycles or treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity; your consultant must specify the planned duration and review point.
admin: Dacarbazine is infused intravenously over 1 hour with protection from light. The total visit also includes safety review, prescribed anti-sickness medicines and observation.
scope: This is dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² over 1 hour, not the 1 g/m² comparator used in some later trials. The current catalogue-linked NCCP document is version 2, reviewed March 2021 with a printed review-due date in March 2026; the treating team should confirm the current local protocol.
consent: Discuss the treatment goal, alternatives including supportive care, uncertainty of benefit, common and serious risks, lasting effects and individual priorities. Record questions and the agreed plan. This is dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² over 1 hour, not the 1 g/m² comparator used in some later trials. The current catalogue-linked NCCP document is version 2, reviewed March 2021 with a printed review-due date in March 2026; the treating team should confirm the current local protocol.
generic: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste change, diarrhoea or constipation; tiredness, hair and skin changes; infusion reactions and intravenous-line complications; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. Risks differ between medicines and people. The medicine-specific section explains the main additional risks for this regimen.

agents.name: Dacarbazine
agents.explanation: Dacarbazine is converted in the body into substances that damage DNA and make it harder for cancer cells to divide. It also affects some healthy cells, including blood-forming cells. This explains why nausea prevention and blood-count checks are central to the plan.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, persistent vomiting, severe upper abdominal pain, new jaundice or rapidly increasing abdominal swelling urgently. Tell the nurse about burning at the infusion site.
risks: Nausea and vomiting; appetite loss and fatigue
Low blood counts with infection, anaemia or bleeding; counts may fall several weeks after a dose
Infusion-site pain and tissue injury if medicine leaks outside the vein
Rare severe liver injury, including blocked small liver veins; severe allergic reactions
Photosensitivity, hair loss and flu-like symptoms; fertility and pregnancy harm; rare later cancers

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: NCCP lists no separate routine premedication or additional regimen-specific prophylaxis, but anti-sickness treatment is required. Bring an up-to-date medicine list and report new abdominal pain, jaundice, fever or bleeding before treatment. This is a high nausea/vomiting-risk treatment. Follow the prescribed prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue plan, and contact the team if vomiting prevents drinking. Confirm any stomach protection and local mouth care. Avoid alcohol and have the team review potentially liver-toxic medicines and phenytoin.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or PICC, agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding as directed. Your team must give written contraception and post-treatment precautions for every medicine, using current product information; the required duration may differ by medicine and between patients.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment, fitness and your priorities. Surgery and radiotherapy may help local control in selected circumstances; their role and timing are decided separately. Chemotherapy does not automatically replace an operation or radiotherapy. Supportive and palliative care can be used alongside cancer treatment to help symptoms and daily life.

support.title: Delayed blood-count and liver effects
support.text: Counts can fall several weeks after dacarbazine. Report fever, bleeding or sudden illness throughout the cycle. Severe upper abdominal pain, yellow eyes or increasing abdominal swelling needs urgent assessment.

monitoring.title: Tests and care through treatment

rows.label: Safety tests and symptoms
cells: Complete baseline checks in the full treatment reference.
Repeat cycle tests and the regimen-specific checks in your written test plan.
Report symptoms promptly; extra tests may be needed.
Follow abnormal results and lasting effects until a plan is agreed.

rows.label: Medicines and practical care
cells: Confirm the written treatment and support prescriptions.
Record actual treatment, support and any safety hold.
Follow the support and contact plan.
Review ongoing support and line-care or removal needs.

rows.label: Cancer treatment and follow-up
cells: Agree the treatment goal and baseline cancer assessment.
Review benefit using the specialist plan.
Report new or changing cancer-related symptoms.
Agree the next sarcoma treatment or follow-up plan.

monitoring.note: Safety testing and cancer-response assessment have different purposes. Your plan may change after illness or a dose adjustment.

tests.label: Full blood count
tests.purpose: Check white cells for infection risk, haemoglobin for anaemia and platelets for bleeding risk.
tests.timing: Before first treatment and before every treatment. Counts may fall several weeks after a dose; infection, bleeding or previous low counts may require extra tests.

tests.label: Kidney and liver tests
tests.purpose: Check safe medicine handling and identify kidney or liver effects.
tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner for symptoms, abnormal results or clinical concerns.

tests.label: Medicines and symptoms
tests.purpose: Check interactions, treatment toxicity and whether support prescriptions are complete.
tests.timing: Before treatment and at each treatment review; report new symptoms or medicine changes between visits.

tests.label: Cancer response and follow-up
tests.purpose: Assess cancer control separately from safety blood tests.
tests.timing: Your consultant sets the scan and clinical-review schedule according to the sarcoma and treatment aim.

evidence.title: Historical EORTC phase II study of high-dose dacarbazine
evidence.summary: A small historical single-arm EORTC study evaluated dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² every three weeks after prior chemotherapy and observed responses in some patients. It supports activity in that setting but does not show a survival advantage over another treatment.
evidence.intro: A small historical single-arm EORTC study evaluated dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² every three weeks after prior chemotherapy and observed responses in some patients. It supports activity in that setting but does not show a survival advantage over another treatment.
evidence.caveat: The historical study used a 20-minute infusion, whereas NCCP 00511 specifies 1 hour. Its small, previously treated population and lack of a randomised comparator limit inference. Do not copy response or survival figures from studies using 1 g/m² or mixed dacarbazine doses as estimates for this exact regimen.
